summary.headline: Lloyds Metals Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 127% YoY to INR5,413 crore with record 39.2% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue reached INR5,413 crore (up 127% YoY, up 10% QoQ), EBITDA INR2,120 crore (up 172% YoY) and PAT INR1,527 crore (up 141% YoY). Management attributes the margin gain to the slurry pipeline cutting logistics costs, higher realisations and a richer value-added mix, with pellets now 41% of standalone revenue. Second pellet plant reached 100% utilisation within four months of its May 2026 commissioning. Thriveni (mining subsidiary) grew revenue 63% YoY but margins were hit by fuel costs, with pass-through negotiations ongoing. Management also outlined large capex (about INR11,000-11,500 crore per year for two years, rising to INR15,000-20,000 crore in year three) and Chemaf/copper JV financing that is still pending.

segments.name: Iron ore (standalone)
segments.commentary: Production 6.05 million tons (+53% YoY), sales 5.46 million tons (+58% YoY); realisation INR6,068/t and EBITDA INR2,230/t. Management said realisation was flat YoY; higher internal consumption reduced merchant sales.

segments.name: DRI and power
segments.commentary: DRI sales 1,83,920 tons (+133% YoY) at INR27,376/t realisation and INR6,273/t EBITDA; power volumes up 87% YoY.

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: Production 1.69 million tons, 100% utilisation within four months of second plant start in May 2026; realisation INR11,783/t, EBITDA INR5,803/t. Sales mix 75.3% domestic, 24.7% export.

segments.name: Thriveni (mining and logistics)
segments.commentary: Iron ore volumes including BHQ 19.09 million tons (nearly 2x from 9.87 million tons). Gadchiroli ROM handling capacity raised from 10 to 55 million tpa; 12.83 million tons produced in the quarter. Odisha volume guided to 34-35 million tons in FY27 (+39%).

segments.name: Copper (Chemaf / JV)
segments.commentary: Existing DRC asset running at about 800 tons per month (about 2,400 tons per quarter); larger JV asset carries about $800 million+ book size and needs about $300 million+ more capex, targeted for operation in Q1 FY28.

guidance_outlook: Thriveni FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 28-30% reiterated, though the Q1 figure was impacted by fuel costs; pass-through talks are underway.
Thriveni logistics EBITDA margin expected to rise from 32% to 40% via EV/LNG fleet shift (200 more vehicles, 50 LNG and 150 EV).
Odisha iron ore volumes expected at 34-35 million tons in FY27; Laserda-Pacheri (1.5 mtpa) started in Q1 and Dalpahar (3 mtpa) expected Q2 FY27.
Steel plant (1.2 mtpa long products) targeted for commissioning by March 2027; BHQ beneficiation by March 2028 with recovery of 38% vs 35% originally planned.
Chemaf financial closure expected in 3-4 months; debt restructuring expected to cut consolidated debt by about 40-50% (roughly $700-800 million).
capex_capacity: Capex of INR13,513 crore in FY24-FY26 and INR3,005 crore in Q1 FY27; about INR8,500 crore planned for FY27 excluding the Konsari steel project, with INR11,000-11,500 crore over the next two years.
Capex guidance for year three is INR15,000-20,000 crore, with further increase once the steel plant is included; copper PNG (Panguna) project excluded and still at study stage.
Foreign (copper JV) capex of about $300 million+ to be spent over the next nine months, with financing (equity and debt) closure expected in about three months.
BHQ beneficiation: 30 million tpa throughput across 9 modules, about 16-17 million tons of saleable output in two phases.
Pellet conversion ratio about 1.07 t iron ore per t pellet; pellet to DRI about 1.5; about 2 t iron ore per t steel.
demand_pricing: Iron ore realisation flat at about INR6,000/t YoY; management said pricing is unpredictable and is not forecasting it.
Pellet export mix about 25%; export markets include Kenya, South Africa, South Korea, Indonesia and China; about 3/4 domestic and 1/4 export by volume.
Slurry pipeline saves about INR500-550/t on pellet cost.
About 2.4 million tons of iron ore and pellet to be consumed internally by FY28 (1.4 million additional for the steel plant), per management.
Thriveni external contracts: Tata Steel MDO volume 3-4 million tons; NTPC and OMC contracts growing 3-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did iron ore EBITDA per ton stay flat despite 58% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales price stayed around INR6,000/t and more ore was used internally, so merchant sales volume and per-ton margin in the reported figure did not rise; the margin shifted to value-added products.

qa_highlights.question: Is the pellet margin structural or one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slurry pipeline saves about INR550/t, export share is expected to stay around 25%, and the margin gains are structural rather than cyclical.

qa_highlights.question: NTPC wage receivable of about INR300 crore: why no provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no provision is planned; the arbitration award was won, NTPC has not accepted it, the matter is sub judice, and resolution is hoped for in 2-3 months. Management also said NTPC relations remain sound with a new contract awarded.

qa_highlights.question: Chemaf debt restructuring: will consolidated debt fall by $700-800 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said restructuring will complete in the next quarter before creditor deadlines, and debt will fall significantly, by about 40-50%, though some new debt may replace old debt.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR650 crore raised in Thriveni?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said proceeds are to refinance high-cost debt, fund conversion of conventional equipment to electric equipment and fund overseas subsidiaries for mining; Thriveni's blended interest cost is about 9-9.5% and Q1 interest was about INR115 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What about the DRC copper export ban?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the DRC exports mainly cathode, and both assets will produce final cathodes, so there is no impact on them.

risks_watch: Iron ore pricing and pellet realisation are cyclical; management declined to guide on pricing and margins beyond FY27.
Thriveni margins fell due to higher fuel costs; pass-through agreements with clients are still under negotiation.
NTPC receivable of about INR300 crore is unprovided and under arbitration; outcome and timing uncertain.
Copper JV: $300 million+ capex and financing closure still pending; Chemaf debt restructuring not yet complete; management declined to disclose copper margins or timing of profitability.
Steel plant and Panguna (PNG) copper projects not board-approved; capex beyond FY27 is not finalised.
summary.management_tone: Confident and celebratory on the quarter's results and margins, but evasive on forward pricing, copper margins, PNG and the larger steel plant, saying plans are not yet finalised or are too early to quantify.
key_quotes: I'm proud to say our pellets operations reached 100% capacity utilization within just 4 months.
This is a structural re-rating of the earnings base, not a cyclical spike.

We are confident that these margins can sustain in the cyclical commodity because we continue to actively pursue better and higher value markets for every product we make, chasing realization and not just volume.
Our teams are evaluating and making a plan on how we can increase the production capacity in these mines over the next 3 to 5 years.
